In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement and interpretation of the Young's modulus of CS and VPS monolithic coatings.
the development of a novel method to measure dynamic elastic moduli of metallic coatings at elevated temperatures.
the measurement of Young's modulus as a function of temperature of monolithic CS and VPS metallic coatings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CS process is not suitable for fabricating high strength metallic coatings.
the Young's modulus of CS and VPS coatings is a function of temperature and the microstructure of the coatings.

Young's moduli of the monolithic metallic coatings studied in this work decreased with increasing temperature and the CS Cu–8%Al had the highest modulus followed by CS Cu–23Cr–5% Al, VPS NiCr, CS NiCrAlY and VPS Cu–23%Al.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dynamic elastic modulus data for cold sprayed metallic coatings are generally in good agreement with the literature data compiled from other techniques, except that the data for CS Cu–23Cr–5Al are about 10% lower than the literature data for the same material deposited by the vacuum plasma spray process.
the Young's modulus data for the CS and VPS Cu–23% Cr–5%Al coatings are consistent with the published data for the bulk material.
the Young's modulus data for cold spray and vacuum plasma spray monolithic metallic coatings are in good agreement with each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Young's modulus data of metallic coatings can be used as a means of assessing the degree of cold work of the coating material.
the dynamic elastic modulus property of a metallic coating is a strong function of its microstructural features.
the Young's modulus of the VPS and CS coatings are similar at room temperature, but the CS coatings are significantly more compliant than the VPS coatings at high temperatures.
